results.claim: The executable parsed-command set starts empty, so an authority check that throws leaves nothing executable. Restoring the historical initialization from parsedCommands makes every parsed command executable again on error.
The batch is atomic: commands approved before a failing evaluation are not kept. Publishing each approval as it is made keeps the approved prefix executable.

A verdict that does not state a boolean allowed, a boolean requiresApproval and a recognized tier is a failed authority check. Without that check a truthy non-boolean is read as an approval, an allowed with no approval semantics is read as an approval, and a verdict with no allowed is read as an ordinary denial that keeps the rest of the batch.
STEP_5_CHECK_AUTONOMY names a failed authority check as authority_check_failed_closed. Reporting it with the outcome of an ordinary evaluation hides the failure behind zero approvals.

AUTH-FC-F1. allowed: true is not an approval unless the verdict also states requiresApproval and a recognized tier. Restoring the validator of 65706fcc, which checked only a boolean allowed, lets a verdict with the approval semantics left out be read as an explicit non-approval-required allow, and the command executes.
AUTH-FC-F1. requiresApproval must be stated as a boolean. Without that check a verdict that omits it, or carries a falsy non-boolean, is read as no approval required.
AUTH-FC-F1. tier must be one of manual, supervised or full. Without that check a verdict with no tier, or with a tier this code does not know, is read as not manual.

With no authority oracle the local fallback is a complete, ordinary non-executable verdict. If it does not state its tier the stricter validator rejects it and the absence of an oracle is reported as authority_check_failed_closed instead of an ordinary evaluation.
